title: Southern Wu
capsule: Southern Wu (南吳, Nán Wú), also called Yang Wu, was one of the Ten Kingdoms that emerged in the lower Yangtze region after the collapse of the Tang dynasty, founded by the warlord Yang Xingmi (r. 902–905) who controlled Huainan and had been recognised by the Tang court as Prince of Wu. Power quickly passed to the regent family of the Xu clan, who effectively ruled in the name of the Yang monarchs for over two decades before Xu Zhigao deposed the last Yang ruler in 937 and renamed himself Li Bian, founding the successor Southern Tang state. Southern Wu occupied much of the Jiangnan (lower Yangtze) region, with its capital at Guangling (modern Yangzhou), and represents a transitional phase between Tang regional governorship and the fully independent kingdoms of the Five Dynasties period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Southern Wu's core territory in the Huai and lower Yangtze basin is reasonably well attested from Song-era histories, but precise boundary lines with neighboring kingdoms are approximate and subject to scholarly disagreement.
